note: A thin, identity-only lexical reference for the optical-transport configuration case. One entry per concept: a stable id, a preferred label, synonyms, a shallow class, a disambiguating definition, and a single canonical example. Deliberately small and not a model of the domain.

entries.label: forwarding vertex
entries.definition: A device that forwards traffic and terminates links in the fabric.

entries.label: span cap
entries.definition: The point on a vertex where a topological span terminates.
entries.example: the R1 end of the R1-R2 span

entries.label: tier bridging
entries.definition: A relationship in which one tier is carried over, or adapts to, another.
entries.example: grd2 adapted into an crr4 server tier at R1

entries.label: run cap
entries.definition: The origination or cap of a run or conduit, i.e. the head of an end-to-end path.
entries.example: the head of the A1-A3 grd2 conduit at A1

entries.label: client offer access
entries.definition: The point at which an external client offer accesses the network.
entries.example: the grd2 client hand-off at access vertex A1

entries.label: circuit offer
entries.definition: An end-to-end carriage offer realised across the network.

entries.label: multiplex structure
entries.definition: The structure by which a signal is multiplexed into a server tier.
entries.example: grd2 mapped into carrier slots of an crr4

entries.label: switching constraint
entries.definition: A constraint on which ports or signals may be switched to which within a vertex.

entries.label: topological span
entries.definition: A span between two nodes in the fabric.

entries.label: fabric
entries.definition: The graph of nodes and links that describes the network.

entries.label: circuit endpoint
entries.definition: An endpoint of a circuit within a vertex, bound to a offer.
entries.example: the circuit endpoint for the A1-A3 offer on R1
